learning: Iterations 5, 8 and 9 show that wheel_radius steps of 0.005 m raise s-bend progress by about 0.003 with max_error held. Mass 0.5 kg (iteration 6) and track 0.14 m (iteration 7) both lowered progress. If max_error exceeds 0.069 on any track, speed has reached its useful limit at this controller setting, and the fallback is wheel_radius 0.04 m.
notes: Repeatability package for the Builder's wheel_radius 0.044 m confirmation. Geometry matches iteration 9 exactly and the controller is unchanged, so this race tests whether the iteration 9 gain holds across seeds. Watch slalom and s-bend max_error against the 0.069 band.
rationale: Iteration 9 (wheel_radius 0.044 m, all else as iteration 8) is the best result so far at 52.14. Progress rose on the s-bend (0.158 to 0.1604) and slalom (0.1075 to 0.110). Max_error was 0.062 (oval), 0.0617 (s-bend) and 0.0676 (slalom), all under the 0.069 band, and the slalom is the tightest margin. Every earlier test of gains, sensor span, footprint, lead, body, track and mass left max_error almost unchanged, and the only lever that consistently raised progress was wheel radius. The Builder asks for a repeatability check of this geometry, so I keep the controller byte-identical to iteration 9 (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Any change in the result is then attributable to the geometry and the seed, not to a controller edit. I add noise_robustness and controller_errors to the measurements, because the final track is unseen and robustness to the fixed motor mismatch and sensor noise now matters more than a small progress gain. I expect s-bend progress at or above 0.158, slalom at or above 0.110, and max_error at or below 0.069 on every track.
